subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus
subsystems.role: carries the mission to Mars, powers it and controls its orientation.

subsystems.name: Science instruments
subsystems.role: maps Phobos and Deimos and selects a safe sampling site.

subsystems.name: Sampler
subsystems.role: collects at least ten grams of regolith from Phobos.

subsystems.name: Rover
subsystems.role: drives across the low-gravity surface ahead of the lander to study the regolith.

subsystems.name: Return capsule
subsystems.role: protects the sample during high-speed re-entry and landing on Earth.

subsystems.name: Communication and navigation
subsystems.role: tracks the spacecraft and sends commands across deep space.

buildSteps.title: Design the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Engineers size the bus, propulsion and power for a round trip to Mars and back.

buildSteps.title: Build the instruments
buildSteps.detail: Camera, altimeter and spectrometers are assembled and calibrated in clean rooms.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the sampler and rover
buildSteps.detail: The pneumatic corer and the small rover are fitted and tested with the lander.

buildSteps.title: Launch
buildSteps.detail: A heavy-lift rocket places the spacecraft on a trajectory that will catch up with Mars.

buildSteps.title: Cruise and arrive
buildSteps.detail: After a cruise of several months, the spacecraft enters orbit around Mars and then moves into quasi-satellite orbits around Phobos.

buildSteps.title: Operate at Phobos
buildSteps.detail: The rover is released, the surface is surveyed, and the spacecraft touches down briefly to fire the corer into the regolith and seal the sample.

buildSteps.title: Return and recover
buildSteps.detail: The spacecraft leaves Mars, releases the capsule near Earth, and the sample is recovered after re-entry and parachute landing.

prerequisites.why: the mission needs enough speed to escape Earth and reach Mars with a return stage still attached.
long-range radio links are needed to navigate and command the spacecraft.
Japan has already returned asteroid samples, proving the re-entry and recovery chain.
small rovers have been dropped onto asteroids, but driving on a moon with some gravity is different.
the sampling mechanism is being developed and must work in vacuum and low gravity.
these orbits near a small moon are delicate and must be controlled for months.

pathway.milestone: final integration and testing of the spacecraft
rover deployment and sample collection on Phobos
pathway.unlocks: the first material from a Martian moon.

pathway.milestone: return to Earth and sample recovery
pathway.unlocks: laboratory analysis of Phobos regolith and any embedded Martian rock.

pathway.milestone: comparison of Phobos samples with Martian meteorites
pathway.unlocks: better understanding of the moons' origin and of Mars's surface history.
